a3:T2c4c,# Relates to

Repairs the evidence-loss mode recorded in the `cloud / agent-stability / deterministic-keyless` failure on develop ([job 110656869424](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/36947981894/job/110656869424)): attempt 01 was killed at its wall-clock timeout, and the trajectory artifact upload (`Upload deterministic trajectories and ledgers`, `if-no-files-found: error`) then failed with `EACCES: permission denied ... child-runtime-ledger.json`, so the run's trajectory and ledger evidence was never uploaded. Complements #32998, which restores graceful scenario teardown; this PR closes the remaining artifact-readability gap for attempts that are still killed abnormally.

# Change

- `packages/cloud/scripts/e2e/stability-attempt.ts`: extends the already-merged parent-owned pre-creation pattern (previously covering only the quiescence ledger) to the child network ledger and the synthetic runtime ledger, with the mechanism documented inline: a ledger the child creates itself — or publishes by renaming a file from its private tmpfs, which carries no default ACL — ends up owned by the ephemeral sandbox UID with mode 0600 and becomes unreadable to the uploader after an abnormal exit.
- `packages/testing/scenario-runner/src/runtime-factory.ts`: when the launcher pre-created the evidence file, `writeSyntheticRuntimeEvidence` now updates that inode in place instead of renaming a child-owned tmp file over it. Fresh creates keep the existing tmp+rename path and 0600 creation mode. The 1 MiB reject-before-write bound is unchanged.

Material risk: minimal. The writer's only reader is the controller after child exit, so sequential in-place writes preserve the existing contract (a malformed or missing ledger still invalidates the attempt under the existing J3 handling); the pre-created empty network ledger parses to zero entries through the existing split/filter consumer.

# Evidence Details

<details>
<summary>Failure mechanism (from the recorded CI run)</summary>

The synthetic runtime evidence writer published its ledger by writing a private tmp file inside the sandbox and `renameSync`-ing it into the output directory. Files created inside the launcher-mounted output directory inherit the launcher's default ACL (granting the controller read), but the tmpfs inside bubblewrap carries no default ACL, so the renamed file kept `0600` owned by the ephemeral sandbox UID. After a hard kill at the attempt wall-clock timeout, the launcher's ACL cleanup could not make that file readable, and the `if-no-files-found: error` trajectory upload aborted with EACCES — destroying the run's most valuable evidence precisely on the failure path where it matters. The pre-existing quiescence-ledger repair (in-place `writeFile`, merged on develop) already models the correct pattern; this change completes it for the remaining two ledgers and pins the writer-side invariant with a real-inode regression test.

</details>

- `gepa-planner-case-process.test.ts` (8 tests) and 2 `stack-partial-cleanup`/`stability-scenario-child` tests fail in this sandbox identically with and without this change; they are recorded here per the template rather than silently skipped.

a4:T20af,# Relates to

`resolveOwnerEntityId` (`packages/core/src/owner-entity.ts`) resolves the owner for LifeOps owner routing (`dispatch-context.ts`, `runtime-wiring.ts`, `service-mixin-core.ts`), the proactive worker, escalation and the relationships graph. Every other owner surface goes through `resolveOwnerEntityIdOrDefault` (`roles.ts`), which accepts the configured owner only when it is a UUID and otherwise uses `deterministicOwnerEntityId(agentId)`. `resolveOwnerEntityId` could return a non-UUID from two places:

- The room scan returned a world's `metadata.ownership.ownerId` verbatim. Legacy connector worlds can hold a platform id there (a Discord snowflake, for example), which `resolveCanonicalOwnerId` already rejects with `validateUuid`.
- The configured-owner branch returned `resolveCanonicalOwnerId(runtime)` without `validateUuid`, so a non-UUID `ELIZA_ADMIN_ENTITY_ID` came back verbatim. `packages/agent/src/api/client-chat-admin.ts` already warns about that setting (`Invalid agents.defaults.adminEntityId … using deterministic fallback`). @Prabhat1308 found this branch in review.

Either way the resolver disagrees with every other surface, and the first UUID-typed query fails. On PGlite, `getRoomsForParticipants(["123456789012345678"])` throws `invalid input syntax for type uuid`.

No linked issue; found in a self-audit.

# Change

- Room scan: `validateUuid` the world's `ownership.ownerId`, skip an invalid world and keep scanning. When no world yields a UUID, the existing deterministic fallback applies. (08d89b29)
- Configured owner: when an owner is configured, return `resolveOwnerEntityIdOrDefault(runtime)` and never enter the world scan. A world owner cannot override operator config, and a non-UUID configured id gets the same deterministic fallback every other surface uses. (44baa38d, review follow-up)
- Test: the stub-runtime unit test is replaced by `owner-entity.pglite.test.ts`, a real `AgentRuntime` on in-memory PGlite (`@elizaos/plugin-sql`), set up like `services/embedding.activation-retry.pglite.test.ts`.
- Risk: a deployment with a non-UUID configured owner used to get that string back from this resolver. It now gets the deterministic owner id that client chat and LifeOps already write under. Valid UUIDs resolve as before.

a9:Tdf3,## Problem

Four code-fence patterns in the model-output parsing path spell the info string `(?:json|json5)?`. Everything after that group (`\s*\r?\n?`) can match empty, so on a ```` ```json5 ```` fence the regex engine takes the `json` branch, the overall match still succeeds, and the captured body starts with the leftover `5` (e.g. `5\n{"a": 1}`). Every downstream parser then rejects it:

| Site | Effect of a ```` ```json5 ```` fenced response |
|---|---|
| `packages/core/src/text/model-output.ts` (`jsonBlockPattern`) | `parseJSONObjectFromText` returns `null`; `extractAndParseJSONObjectFromText` throws |
| `plugins/plugin-calendar/src/internal/detail.ts` (`MODEL_CODE_FENCE_PATTERN`) | `parseCalendarJsonRecord` returns `null` |
| `plugins/plugin-inbox/src/inbox/priority-scoring.ts` (`STRUCTURED_CODE_FENCE_PATTERN`) | the whole scoring batch fails ("did not return JSON scores or a legacy JSON array") |
| `plugins/plugin-inbox/src/inbox/triage-classifier.ts` (`TRIAGE_CODE_FENCE_PATTERN`) | legacy array triage throws "did not return a JSON array" |

The shared helper `unwrapWholeCodeFence` (`packages/core/src/utils/code-fence.ts`) already handles this correctly by trying labels longest-first.

## Fix

List the longer label first — `(?:json5|json)?` — at all four sites, and drop the duplicated `json|json` alternative in `priority-scoring.ts`. `plugins/plugin-assistant/src/runtime/evaluator.ts:2066` uses the same ordering but is left unchanged: it only parses the trailing object, so a leftover `5` stays in the preceding prose and is harmless there.

## Prior work

The JSON5-label defect was reported in #30536 (@attentionhead), which a maintainer confirmed as real and consolidated into #30875 (@hermesagent270-commits). #30875 was closed on 2026-09-26 because the package restructure moved the affected files, with a request to open a fresh PR against the current layout if still needed. This is that fresh PR against the current paths; credit for the diagnosis goes to both.

## Verification

- `packages/core/src/text/model-output.test.ts` (new): `json5` / JSON5-only syntax / uppercase `JSON5` / `json` / unlabeled fences parse to the object; a `json5`-fenced array is extracted without throwing.
- `plugins/plugin-calendar/test/detail.test.ts`: added a ```` ```json5 ```` case to `parseCalendarJsonRecord`.
- `plugins/plugin-inbox/src/inbox/priority-scoring.test.ts`: a ```` ```json5 ````-fenced `{"scores":[…]}` response is scored and `reportError` is not called.
- `plugins/plugin-inbox/test/triage-code-fence.test.ts` (new): a ```` ```json5 ````-fenced legacy array is classified by `classifyMessages`.
- Red→green: every new case fails on `develop` with the effects in the table above and passes with the fix; the `json` / unlabeled controls pass both ways.
- Full `plugin-inbox` suite: 296 passed. `plugin-calendar` full suite: identical results with and without this change (its pre-existing failures come from unbuilt workspace packages in my environment).
- `tsc --noEmit` (test files included) and Biome clean on the changed files.

`AgentRuntime.runActionsByMode` runs mode hooks (`ALWAYS_BEFORE`, `ALWAYS_DURING`, `ALWAYS_AFTER`, `CONTEXT_*`, `RESPONSE_HANDLER_*`) and reports each one through `ACTION_COMPLETED` with `actionStatus`. ab:T1073,# Relates to

`TaskService.runDueTasks()` loads the queue and runs `runTick` without coordinating with the local interval tick (`activeTick`). No production runtime sets `serverless: true`, so the 1-second timer is always running while the app's wake routes call `runDueTasks()` on the same service:

- `POST /api/internal/wake` (`packages/app/src/api/internal-routes.ts`), driven by the Android WorkManager worker and the iOS background plugin.
- `POST /api/background/run-due-tasks` (`packages/app/src/api/background-tasks-routes.ts`).

Each route only merges its own concurrent calls. When a wake lands while a timer tick is executing a due one-shot task, which is likely when a suspended process thaws and both fire, the wake reads the queue before the one-shot is deleted and runs it again. The one-shot branch of `runTick` has no `executingTasks` guard, so the user gets a duplicate reminder or follow-up.

# Change

`runDueTasks` waits for any in-flight tick, then registers its own run as `activeTick`, clearing it when done. Timer ticks already skip while `activeTick` is set, so host wakes and timer ticks now run one at a time, and each reads the queue after the previous run has committed its deletes and reschedules. `stop()` already awaits `activeTick`, so it now waits for an in-flight wake too. Errors still reach the `runDueTasks` caller unchanged.

# Testing

New `packages/core/src/services/task-wake-overlap.pglite.test.ts` uses `createTestRuntime` (real SQL task storage) and a virtual clock that captures the timer callback. It starts a timer tick whose one-shot worker blocks, calls `runDueTasks()` concurrently, releases the worker, and expects exactly one execution with the task deleted.

- On develop: `AssertionError: expected 2 to be 1`.
- With this change it passes. Together with `task-wake.pglite.test.ts` and `task.pause-race.pglite.test.ts`: 3 files, 13 tests passed.
- `biome check` on the changed files is clean, and `tsc --noEmit` in `packages/core` reports nothing for them.

ad:T17d9,# Relates to

#32991 (preserve nullable action arguments) made core tool-argument validation reject an explicit `null` for an optional parameter whose schema does not admit null. That is deliberate policy, pinned by a test in the follow-up `2f8202f39d`. [This review](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/pull/32991#pullrequestreview-5378778041) flagged the BLOCK action as a shipped caller that still asks for null, and it is unchanged on develop `811c3fac48`:

```ts
name: "durationMinutes",
description: "Block duration minutes. Omit/null = indefinite until manual removal.",
schema: { type: "number" },
```

- **The description is the model's instruction.** A non-strict provider that follows it and sends `durationMinutes: null` gets `Argument 'durationMinutes' expected number, got null`, and the call fails. This applies to `BLOCK` and to the promoted `BLOCK_*` actions, which share the parameter.
- **Omission already means indefinite.** When the message states no duration, the website handler's text heuristic finds none and the app handler's plan has none, so the block runs until manual removal.

# Change

- **Description only:** `durationMinutes` now reads "Block duration in minutes. Omit to block until manually removed." The schema stays `{ type: "number" }`.
- **Why not admit null** (the first revision of this PR): in OpenAI strict mode models must send every key and use `null` for "no value".
  - Develop drops that null (`restoreOmittedOptionalKeys`), so the handler still reads a duration from the message text.
  - A schema that admits null would keep it as "indefinite", turning "block x.com for 2 hours" into an indefinite draft whenever the model filled the key with null.
  - Changing only the description keeps the strict path exactly as it is. Thanks @Prabhat1308 for catching that.
- **A guard test for the class:** for `BLOCK` and every promoted `BLOCK_*` action, no parameter description may ask for `null` while its schema rejects null.

# Testing

</details>af:T115f,# Relates to

`installRuntimePluginLifecycle` wraps `registerModel` to record which model handlers a plugin owns, so that `unloadPlugin` and `reloadPlugin` can remove them. It recorded `models.get(type).slice(modelsBefore)`, which assumes the new entry is appended. `ModelDispatcher.registerModel` inserts and then sorts by priority (highest first), so when a higher-priority provider registers after a default-priority one, the tail is the other plugin's handler.

Eliza Cloud registers its text models at priority 50, and provider plugins default to 0. With a local provider loaded:

- **Disabling Eliza Cloud** (`PUT /api/plugins/:id` → `applyPluginRuntimeMutation` → `unloadPlugin`) removes the local provider's `TEXT_LARGE` handler and leaves Cloud's registered. The settings page shows Cloud as disabled while chat keeps routing to Cloud.
- **Reloading the Cloud plugin** leaves two Cloud handlers. A later unload removes both, so the agent is left with "This agent has no model provider configured" even though the local provider plugin is still loaded.

# Change

The wrapper snapshots the registration records that existed before the call and records, by identity, every record that is new afterwards, wherever the priority sort put it. The other ownership captures (actions, providers, evaluators, events) are append-only and unchanged.

# Testing

New `packages/core/src/__tests__/plugin-lifecycle-model-priority.test.ts` uses a real `AgentRuntime` with a default-priority `local-llm` and a priority-50 `cloud-llm` provider:

- After the unload, the ownership is `["cloud-llm"]`, `TEXT_LARGE` keeps only `local-llm`, and `getModel` returns the local handler.
- A reload keeps exactly `["cloud-llm", "local-llm"]`, and a later unload leaves `local-llm`.

Both fail on develop (`expected [ 'local-llm' ] to deeply equal [ 'cloud-llm' ]` and `expected [ 'cloud-llm', 'cloud-llm' ] to deeply equal [ 'cloud-llm', 'local-llm' ]`) and pass with this change. `src/__tests__` plus the core suites that exercise `registerPlugin`/`registerModel` give 17 files and 558 tests passing on the pinned Node 24.15.0. `biome check` and `tsc --noEmit` report nothing for the changed files.

- [x] Targets `develop` and has no conflicts with the latest `origin/develop`.
- [ ] Ran `bun install` and `bun run verify` after syncing; record blockers below.
- [ ] Updated relevant documentation.

b0:T1263,# Relates to

Scheduled workflow triggers dispatch with a per-occurrence idempotency key, `${workflowId}:${minuteBucket(nextRunAtMs)}`, which `executeTriggerTask` refreshes after each run. When `WORKFLOW_DISPATCH` reports `dedup: true`, `executeTriggerTask` returns `skipped` immediately without persisting anything. #22790 added that early return so a replayed native event isn't counted as a new run, but it also catches scheduler and manual fires:

- `nextRunAtMs` and the idempotency key don't advance, and no `updateInterval` is returned.
- The workflow dispatcher looks keys up in durable execution rows that never expire. So every later fire carries the same stale key, is deduplicated again, and the trigger never runs again.

Two ordinary ways in: two triggers on one workflow landing in the same minute (a monthly trigger on the 1st and a Mondays trigger when the 1st is a Monday), or a failure after dispatch but before the metadata write, after which `TaskService`'s retry reuses the key.

# Change

The early return stays for `source === "event"`. For scheduler and manual fires, a deduplicated dispatch now re-reads the live task, advances the trigger to its next occurrence with `buildTriggerMetadata`, refreshes the key, persists it, and returns `skipped` with the new `updateInterval`. `runCount`, the run log and notifications are untouched, so a deduplicated fire still isn't counted as a run. The key derivation is shared with the normal persist path through a small helper.

# Testing

New `packages/agent/src/triggers/trigger-dedup-advance.test.ts` runs a Mondays cron trigger through the real `executeTriggerTask`. The dispatch service deduplicates repeated keys, the trigger's key has already been used for Jun 1, and the clock is faked.

- On develop: the Jun 1 fire returns no `updateInterval` (`expected 'undefined' to be 'number'`), the schedule stays at Jun 1, and the Jun 8 fire is deduplicated again.
- With this change: the Jun 1 fire is skipped and advances to Jun 8, and the Jun 8 fire runs (`executions: ["2026-06-08T09:00:01.000Z"]`).
- The agent trigger tests pass 8/8 on the pinned Node 24.15.0, and plugin-workflow's `trigger-routes`, `trigger-ownership` and `workflow-dispatch` suites pass 20/20.
- `biome check` on the changed files is clean, and `tsc --noEmit` reports nothing for `src/triggers`.

b2:T124f,# Relates to

Messages whose text or attachments exceed the 64 KB inline cap are stored as a parent row plus `message_content_segments` rows that hold the full content. The segments link back through `metadata.messageId`; see `persistMessageMemory` → `createMessageMemory` → `publishMessageContentSegments`, used for inbound and response messages in plugin-assistant.

All three adapter delete paths (`deleteMemory`, `deleteManyMemories`, `deleteAllMemories`) cascade only through `getMemoryFragments`, which matches `metadata.documentId`. Deleting a large message therefore removes the parent row and leaves the full text behind, whether it comes from deleting a conversation message (`conversation-message-service.ts`), clearing a channel (`deleteAllMemories([roomId], "messages")`), deleting a single message, or the memory-retention sweep. The leftover rows still show up in `listMemoryTypes`, and agent export copies every type, so "deleted" message text ends up in exported bundles.

# Change

`getMemoryFragments` also matches `message_content_segments` rows whose `metadata.messageId` is the deleted memory's id. Every delete path already goes through this helper, so segments are now removed in the same transaction as their parent. The query is covered by the existing partial index `idx_message_content_byte_seek` on `(agent_id, metadata->>'messageId', …)`.

# Testing

b4:T11ae,# Relates to

After the user clicks Disconnect in Settings, `POST /api/cloud/disconnect` returns `{"ok":true,"status":"disconnected"}` and status shows disconnected, but the running agent keeps resolving the old `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_API_KEY`. Its Cloud text-model handlers (`getApiKey` / `createCloudApiClient` → `runtime.getSetting`) keep sending prompts to `api.eliza.app` with `Bearer <old key>`, billed to the org, until the agent restarts. Meanwhile the disconnect dialog tells the user the agent will need a local provider.

Cause:

- Login persist (`cloud-routes.ts`) calls `runtime.setSetting("ELIZAOS_CLOUD_API_KEY", key)`, and does the same for `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_USER_ID` and `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_ORG_ID`. Those calls write `character.settings` and the runtime's settings map.
- `clearRuntimeCloudState` deletes the key from `character.secrets`, but its setting cleanup list (`CLOUD_RUNTIME_SETTING_KEYS`) only holds the `ELIZA_CLOUD_*` aliases. The `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_*` settings copies survive.

# Change

`CLOUD_RUNTIME_SETTING_KEYS` now also covers `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_API_KEY`, `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_ENABLED`, `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_USER_ID` and `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_ORG_ID`, so the existing `setSetting(key, null)` loop removes both the settings copy and the runtime settings copy. The two identity keys are also added to `CLOUD_RUNTIME_SECRET_KEYS`. Nothing else changes.

# Relates to

Two agent actions still report success on a 2xx response they never confirmed, the same defect 6beb04b5c1 fixed for PLUGIN configure today. Both are registered in production through `packages/agent/src/runtime/eliza-plugin.ts` (`promoteSubactionsToActions(logsAction)`, `promoteSubactionsToActions(runtimeAction)`), and both calls pass the real `validateToolArgs`, so planner calls reach the handlers.

- **LOGS `delete`** (`packages/agent/src/actions/logs.ts` `deleteLogs`): `(await resp.json().catch(() => ({})))` plus `cleared` defaulting to `0` turns a proxy HTML page, `{}`, or `{"cleared":"lots"}` into `success: true`, "Cleared 0 log entries.". The route (`diagnostics-routes.ts` `DELETE /api/logs`) always answers `{ cleared: <count> }`.
- **RUNTIME `reload_config`** (`packages/agent/src/actions/runtime.ts` `reloadConfigOp`): any 2xx JSON is success and `applied`/`requiresRestart` default to `[]`, so `{}` or `{"reloaded":false}` tells the owner "No hot-reloadable fields changed.". The route (`server-lazy-routes.ts` `POST /api/config/reload`) answers `{ reloaded: true, applied, requiresRestart }`.

Real handlers on develop `27dec7b0c3`, fetch stubbed:

```
LOGS delete body=<html>proxy</html> -> {"success":true,"text":"Cleared 0 log entries."}
LOGS delete body={} -> {"success":true,"text":"Cleared 0 log entries."}
LOGS delete body={"cleared":"lots"} -> {"success":true,"text":"Cleared 0 log entries."}
RUNTIME reload_config body={} -> {"success":true,"text":"No hot-reloadable fields changed."}
RUNTIME reload_config body={"reloaded":false} -> {"success":true,"text":"No hot-reloadable fields changed."}
```

# Change

- LOGS delete parses the body in a J3-annotated `try`, requires a plain object with a non-negative integer `cleared`, and otherwise returns `LOGS_DELETE_FAILED` ("the server did not confirm the clear").
- RUNTIME reload_config requires `reloaded === true` and string arrays for `applied` and `requiresRestart` (`isReloadConfigAcknowledgement`), otherwise `RUNTIME_RELOAD_CONFIG_FAILED`. A non-JSON 2xx body was already caught by the outer `try`; only the shape check was missing.
- Genuine acknowledgements (including a real `{ cleared: 0 }` and an acknowledged reload that changed nothing) behave exactly as before.

b6:Tfe6,## Problem

`ELIZA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_MIGRATIONS` was parsed with two different contracts:

- The migration runners that actually arm destructive schema changes — `packages/core/src/runtime.ts`, `packages/core/src/provisioning.ts`, `packages/agent/src/runtime/plugin-lifecycle.ts`, and `plugins/plugin-sql/src/runtime-migrator/runtime-migrator.ts` — require the exact documented value `true`.
- The boot policy (`resolveBootPolicy` via `environment.isEnabled`, which accepts `1`/`true`/`on`/`yes` case-insensitively) and the restore-generation environment guard (`assertEnvironment`, which accepted the same loose set) treated a much wider set of values as authorized.

Setting the variable to `1` or `TRUE` therefore produced contradictory behavior: boot logged `Destructive database migrations are enabled` and a restored-generation boot was rejected with `AGENT_BACKUP_RESTORE_V3_BOOT_DESTRUCTIVE_MIGRATION_FORBIDDEN`, even though the destructive capability never armed anywhere. An operator recovering an agent from a committed backup generation with a common truthy env value got a false-positive restore failure pointing at a capability that was not active. The comment above the boot warning claimed the runtime and migration layer read the same policy — they demonstrably did not.

## Change

- Add `isExactTrueEnvFlag` to `packages/core/src/utils/env.ts` (next to `isEnvDisabled`) as the single authorization predicate for dangerous opt-in flags whose documented value is exactly `true`.
- Route all six readers of `ELIZA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_MIGRATIONS` through it: core runtime, core provisioning, agent plugin lifecycle, agent boot policy, the restore-generation `assertEnvironment` guard, and the plugin-sql runtime migrator.
- Restore guards now reject a restored boot exactly when the capability can actually arm; truthy-but-undocumented values (`1`, `yes`, `on`, `TRUE`) proceed exactly like an unset variable. No value that previously armed destructive migrations loses that behavior; the arming semantics are unchanged everywhere.
- Correct the stale comment above the boot warning so it states the real contract.

## Validation

- `packages/core`: `bun run typecheck` clean; `bun run test` green (1092 passed, 2 skipped).
- `packages/agent`: `bun run typecheck` clean; `src/runtime/restore-generation.boot.test.ts` green (4 passed) with the new regression cases:
  - the real `startEliza` restore entry with `ELIZA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_MIGRATIONS=1` proceeds past the destructive-migration guard and reaches the genuine `..._BOOT_DATABASE_CONFLICT` failure instead;
  - `authority.assertEnvironment()` accepts `1`/`yes` without throwing and rejects only `true` with `AGENT_BACKUP_RESTORE_V3_BOOT_DESTRUCTIVE_MIGRATION_FORBIDDEN`.
- Red check: with only the two guard sites reverted to the old loose parsing, the new restore assertions fail (`=1` triggers `DESTRUCTIVE_MIGRATION_FORBIDDEN` at the boot-policy guard), proving the test exercises the changed contract.
- `plugins/plugin-sql`: `bun run test` green (27 files, 181 tests).

```
[eliza-autonomous] Failed to start: Error: Runtime state parent is replaceable by another user.
```

The message names neither the failing ancestor (`/home/lumix/.tmp`, mode `0775`,
sticky bit absent in the reproduction), nor its mode, nor the remediation.
Diagnosing it required reading the validation source
(`packages/agent/src/runtime/runtime-installation-id.ts`); every operator whose
state location fails this check is blocked with the same dead end. The sibling
rejections (state directory itself, untrusted owner, non-directory ancestor,
lexical redirect, mobile app-data ancestor) share the gap.

# Change

The module-local trust assertions now include the exact failing path and its
octal mode (plus uids for owner rejections), and the replaceable-parent error
states the remediation (remove group/other write bits or set the sticky bit).
For the reproduction above the same boot now prints:

```
[eliza-autonomous] Failed to start: Error: Runtime state parent /home/lumix/.tmp is replaceable by another user (mode 0775; sticky bit absent). Remove group/other write access or set the sticky bit on this ancestor of the runtime state directory.
```

Throw conditions, validation order, and trust behavior are unchanged — this is
diagnostic context only. Windows (credential-store) and mobile validation logic
are untouched; no other module matches on the previous message strings
(verified by search), and no test pins them.

b8:Tf22,# Relates to

`requireAdminWithResponse` (`packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/auth/admin.ts`) is the auth guard for two admin tools:

- `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/admin/orgs/:orgId/rate-limits`
- `GET /api/v1/admin/users/:userId/billing/breakdown`

It passes the raw `Request` to `requireAdmin(c)` with `request as never`, but `requireAdmin` reads `c.env` and `c.req` from a Hono context. Every call throws a `TypeError` ("undefined is not an object (evaluating 'c.env.NODE_ENV')"), the catch-all maps it to `{"error":"Internal server error"}`, and admins can never read or change org rate-limit overrides or open a user's billing breakdown.

The helper's error mapping is also stale. It checks the legacy `AuthenticationError`/`ForbiddenError` classes from `api/errors`, while `requireAdmin` throws the canonical `ApiError` from `cloud-worker-errors`. Even with the context fixed, a missing session or a non-admin would still get 500 instead of 401 or 403.

# Change

- Both routes pass the Hono context `c` to their handlers and to `requireAdminWithResponse`. The rate-limit PATCH body is read with `c.req.json()`.
- `requireAdminWithResponse` takes `AppContext` and maps canonical `ApiError` statuses 401 and 403. The legacy classes extend it, so they're still covered. The response shape (`{ error }`) is unchanged.

# Testing

New `packages/cloud/api/__tests__/admin-auth-response-context.test.ts` mounts the real rate-limits route with no mocks:

- no credentials in production → expects 401;
- the loopback local-dev admin → expects the handler's own 400 (`Invalid org ID`), which shows auth passed without touching the database.

On develop both requests return 500. With this change both pass (`2 pass, 0 fail`). `biome check` on the changed files is clean, and `tsc --noEmit` in `packages/cloud/{api,shared}` reports nothing for them.

b9:T1597,# Relates to

#33028 (restore declared desktop app window routes) merged with the external-launch path ignoring whether anything opened. That was the blocking point of [this review](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/pull/33028#pullrequestreview-5389020729), and it is unchanged on develop `811c3fac48`.

In `packages/ui/src/components/apps/AppWindowRenderer.routes.tsx`, a catalog app that launches without a viewer URL is opened externally:

```ts
try {
  await openExternalUrl(launchUrl);
} catch {
  /* ignore — we still surface the link state */
}
setRunState({ status: "external", ... });   // → "<app> opened in your browser"
```

`openExternalUrl` (`utils/openExternalUrl.ts:55-102`) resolves `false` when nothing was opened: the URL failed the navigation allowlist (`javascript:`, `data:`, custom schemes), the Electrobun bridge refused or timed out, or no open channel exists. Its doc asks callers handling wire-supplied URLs to show their error state on `false`.

**Result:** the window says "opened in your browser" while nothing opened, and there is no Retry. There is also no `cancelled` check after the `await`, so a window closed during the open still sets state.

# Change

- The open result is checked. `false`, or a rejection, shows the existing launch-error card ("Could not launch …") with the URL and its Retry button.
- `if (cancelled) return;` after the await.
- New string `appwindow.ExternalOpenFailed` ("Could not open this app in your browser: {{url}}"), added to all eight locales like the other `appwindow.*` keys.

The successful path is unchanged.

ba:T1cc1,# Relates to

#32922 (preserve paired turns and recover revoked sessions) made a paired device's streamed turn outlive a dropped SSE socket, but not for devices paired with the operator code. That was the blocking point of [this review](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/pull/32922#pullrequestreview-5346518479), and it is unchanged on develop `811c3fac48`:

- **Only USER sessions get the new behavior.** `conversation-routes.ts` takes the paired-session bearer only for `trustedApiPrincipal.kind === "service_gateway" && sessionRole === "USER"`. Every other caller gets `continueOnDisconnect: false`, so the turn is aborted when the socket closes.
- **Operator-code pairing produces an owner session:**
  - `auth-pairing-routes.ts` sets `pairingAccess = "owner"` when the operator code matches.
  - It then binds the device's machine session to the owner identity (`ensurePairedDeviceIdentityId` → `createMachineSession`).
  - That identity resolves to `OWNER` (`auth.ts` `roleForIdentityKind`), and `resolveTrustedApiPrincipal` returns `{ kind: "owner_session" }` with no `sessionRole` (`chat-routes.ts`).

**Result:** a phone paired with the operator code, which is the usual way to pair your own phone, loses its reply if it goes to the background mid-turn. Nothing is persisted for it to read after reconnecting. `paired-stream-failure-persistence.test.ts` only creates `kind: "machine"` (USER) identities, so it never covered this path.

# Change

`conversation-routes.ts` now resolves the paired-session bearer in one helper, `resolvePairedSessionToken`:

- **USER machine session:** unchanged; the bearer is used as before.
- **`owner_session`:** the bearer is used only if it resolves, through the host bridge's `resolveSessionTokenAuthorization`, to a live session whose identity is the authenticated owner identity.
  - The static API token, the trusted-local bypass and cookie-only sessions do not resolve to a session for that identity, so they keep disconnect-as-cancel.
  - A session-store error also keeps it.
- **Everything else is unchanged:** the 5 s authority recheck, revocation subscription and explicit Stop (`/api/turns/:roomId/abort`) apply to the owner-paired turn exactly as to a USER-paired one.

The pre-check matters. Passing an unchecked bearer to the tracker would make its own authority check fail for, for example, a trusted-local request that also carries the static token, and answer `401 "Paired session ended"` instead of running the turn.

# Testing

1. An identity of `kind: "owner"` gets a machine session, which is what operator-code pairing creates.
2. The device streams a turn and drops the socket mid-generation.

Picking a voice in Settings → Voice saves an explicit ElevenLabs config (`provider: "elevenlabs"`, `mode: "cloud"` or `"own-key"`, plus `elevenlabs.voiceId`). On every later read (`useVoiceConfig.loadVoiceConfig` → `resolveCharacterVoiceConfigFromAppConfig` → the chat and shell voice hooks), `shouldUpdatePresetVoice` replaces the saved voice with the selected character's preset voice whenever the saved voice is the default voice (Sarah) or that character's legacy voice. It does this even when the config is an explicit choice. The file already has `isExplicitElevenLabsChoice` and uses it for the provider-release branch, but not here.

For the characters that ship their own preset voice (Jin, Kei, Momo, Rin, Ryu, Satoshi, Yuki), choosing Sarah, or the character's legacy voice, shows that voice in Settings and sounds right just after Save, but chat speaks the character voice again after the next focus, tab switch or reload.

# Change

The default/legacy migration arm only applies when the stored config is not an explicit ElevenLabs choice. A config with no voice ID still takes the character preset, and legacy configs without a mode or key still migrate as before.

# Relates to

Since #32957 (merged 2026-10-01), `createRedactClone` in `packages/core/src/security/log-redaction.ts` gives every plain and Map/Set clone an own non-enumerable `Symbol.toPrimitive`. Node's `console` hides it, but Bun's prints non-enumerable symbol keys, so under Bun (the agent's runtime) every object in a trailing log argument gets an extra line per nesting level:

```ts
logger.info("probe-console-symbol", { owner: { id: "u1" }, tags: new Map([["a", 1]]) });
```

develop `27dec7b0c3`, Bun 1.4.2 terminal:

```
 Info       probe-console-symbol {
  [Symbol(Symbol.toPrimitive)]: [Function: value],
  owner: {
    [Symbol(Symbol.toPrimitive)]: [Function: value],
    id: "u1",
  },
  tags: {
    [Symbol(Symbol.toPrimitive)]: [Function: value],
    type: "Map",
  ...
```

this branch:

```
 Info       probe-console-symbol {
  owner: {
    id: "u1",
  },
  tags: {
    type: "Map",
    entries: [
      [ "a", 1 ]
    ],
  },
}
```

# Change

The hook exists so a clone that owns a non-callable `toString` copied from source data (`{ toString: "source data" }`) still coerces instead of throwing in sinks such as React DevTools' patched console. Without such a key, the inherited `Object.prototype.toString` already answers, and an own `valueOf` alone is harmless because ToPrimitive falls back to `toString`. So:

- plain clones get the hook only when they own `toString` (checked after their properties are copied);
- Map/Set clones never do (their keys are fixed: `type`, `entries`/`values`);
- Error clones keep it unconditionally, as before (Bun prints errors without it).

A shared prototype carrying the hook does not help: Bun prints inherited `Symbol.toPrimitive` too (checked).

bd:Te49,# Relates to

The Cloud dashboard's analytics page calls `GET /api/analytics/projections`, which runs `generateProjections` and then `generateProjectionAlerts`, and persists `danger` alerts as critical alert events. `generateProjections` stores each projected point as `totalCost: Math.round(costVariance)`. Usage cost is USD with sub-dollar precision (`usage_records` costs are `numeric(16,6)`; #27728 settled that these values are dollars), so every projected day is rounded to whole dollars:

- Flat $0.40/day usage projects as `[0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]`, so the chart shows $0.
- Flat $0.60/day usage projects as `[1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1]`. The alert pass compares that to the $0.60 average and sees a 67% increase, so the user gets a persisted critical "High Cost Projection: Projected costs may increase by 67%" alert for perfectly flat usage.

# Change

Projected `totalCost` keeps the regression value unrounded. Requests and token counts stay integer-rounded.

be:T1ae2,# Relates to

Develop's `canonical / Plugin Tests (3/4)` lane has been red since #32991 landed: at head `3f38e54495ba5518f84bcf9cc1e84e0dc3d60bbf`, `canonical / All Tests Passed` fails with `tests_plugins finished with failure`, and the failing test is `plugins/plugin-personal-assistant/test/work-thread-native-schema.test.ts > WORK_THREAD native arguments (Cerebras: false) > exposes supported operations and preserves sparse lifecycle arguments` (`AssertionError: expected false to be true` at `work-thread-native-schema.test.ts:99`).

# Change

`validateToolArgs` is the admission boundary between model-produced tool arguments and action handlers. #32991 made it validate an explicit `null` against the declared child schema so that schemas which declare nullability (`type: "null"`, nullable enum, `anyOf` null branch) keep the model's explicit null. That preserved intent remains intact.

But strict native-tool grammars require every property, so on the non-Cerebras strict-tool wire an omitted optional argument arrives as explicit `null` — the encoding `plugins/plugin-openai` restores from provider tool calls and `plugins/plugin-personal-assistant/test/work-thread-native-schema.test.ts` pins as a live observed contract ("non-Cerebras strict tools also represent omitted optionals as null"). After #32991, every such restored call failed admission (`workThreadId: null` against `type: "string"` → type error), so WORK_THREAD — and any action with optional parameters called through that path — got rejected before handler execution.

This reconciles both contracts at the same single admission boundary:

- a schema that admits `null` keeps the explicit null (unchanged from #32991);
- a `null` that fails an **optional** property's schema is the wire's absence encoding and resolves like an omitted key (declared default applied, key dropped);
- a `null` on a **required** property still fails through the child-schema type error.

Material risk: a model that emits a spurious `null` for an optional property is now treated as "omitted" rather than rejected. That was the admission behavior on develop before #32991 (and `resolve-action-args.ts`'s `valueIsPresent` already treats `null` as not-present), and it is what the pinned live wire contract requires; strict tools cannot express optional absence any other way.

bf:T1a1b,# Relates to

`buildBoundedNumberRule` (`packages/core/src/runtime/response-grammar.ts`) enumerates small integer ranges (`max - min <= 200`) as a GBNF alternation, but built each alternative with `gbnfJsonStringLiteral`, which JSON-quotes the value. A grammar-guided model could therefore only emit a JSON string where the schema declares an integer. The other branches of the function (unbounded, inverted and wide ranges, floats) use the bare-number `jsonnumber` rule; only this enumeration quoted its values.

Reachable on develop: plugin-assistant's planner (`runtime/planner-loop.ts`) sends `buildPlannerActionGrammarStrict(plannerActions)` as `modelParams.grammar`. plugin-personal-assistant's `TASK_CREATE_PLAN_PARAMETER` (`createPlan`) declares `priority: { type: "integer", minimum: 1, maximum: 5 }` and `dueWeekday: { type: "integer", minimum: 0, maximum: 6 }`. On develop the strict grammar for that parameter only allows `"priority":"3"`, and `parseNativeTaskCreatePlan` rejects a string priority and discards the whole plan. The handler then keeps normal extraction, the second interpretation call that `createPlan` exists to avoid. This applies to engines that enforce the grammar; engines that ignore `grammar` are unaffected.

No linked issue; found in a self-audit.

# Change

- Build each enumerated alternative with `gbnfLiteral(String(i))`, so the rule is `"1" | "2" | "3" | …`, bare JSON numbers like the other branches.
- Risk: a grammar-guided model now emits numbers for these fields, which is what their integer schemas declare.

c2:Teab,# Relates to

`WORKTREE` enter without a `path` builds the worktree directory as `path.join(os.tmpdir(), "eliza-worktree-…")` and registers that raw path with `sandbox.addRoot` and `session.pushWorktree`. `SandboxService.validatePath` compares fully resolved real paths. On macOS `os.tmpdir()` is under `/var/folders/...`, which resolves to `/private/var/folders/...`, so every file inside the new worktree fails validation with `outside_allowed_roots`.

Registering a root also turns on root enforcement for that conversation, so the failure isn't limited to the worktree. FILE read, write, edit, grep and glob, and the SHELL cwd all stop working, even in the default trusted mode with no `CODING_TOOLS_WORKSPACE_ROOTS` configured.

# Change

The auto-generated worktree path goes through the existing `resolveRealPath` (`lib/path-utils.ts`), which resolves the longest existing ancestor (the tmp dir) and rejoins the not-yet-created leaf. `git worktree add`, `addRoot`, `pushWorktree` and the later `exit` all use that one resolved path. Explicit `path` values were already returned resolved by `validatePath` and are unchanged.

# Testing

`src/actions/enter-worktree.test.ts` gains a case that enters an auto-generated worktree and checks that `sandbox.validatePath` accepts a file inside it.

- On develop (macOS): `1 failed | 5 passed`.
- With this change, the enter and exit worktree suites pass 11/11, and the whole plugin passes (`vitest run`: 46 files, 990 tests, 1 skipped).
- `tsc --noEmit` and `biome check` report nothing for the changed files.

c4:T1274,# Relates to

`AgentRuntime.getSetting` reads `character.secrets[key]` before `character.settings[key]`, but `setSetting(key, value, false)` only writes `character.settings` and the constructor settings map. A key that boot placed in `character.secrets` can therefore never be changed or cleared by a non-secret write while the agent runs.

Boot composition (`packages/agent/src/runtime/build-character-config.ts`) copies several keys that aren't credentials into `character.secrets` whenever they are set in the environment, for example `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_BASE_URL`, `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_ENABLED`, `SOLANA_RPC_URL`, `MATTERMOST_BASE_URL` and the `X402_*` flags. Plugins declare some of these as non-sensitive parameters (`ELIZAOS_CLOUD_BASE_URL` and `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_ENABLED` in plugin-elizacloud, `SOLANA_RPC_URL` in auto-trader). When the owner changes one through `PUT /api/plugins/:id`, `persistMutation` calls `runtime.setSetting(key, value|null, param.sensitive=false)`, the plugin applies or reloads, and the route returns `ok: true`. The plugin keeps reading the boot value, for example `cloud-auth.ts` → `getSetting("ELIZAOS_CLOUD_BASE_URL")`, until the agent restarts. Clearing the value is ignored the same way.

`packages/agent/src/runtime/runtime-settings.ts` already works around this precedence by hand for model pins, by deleting matching secret copies before writing.

# Change

When the key already exists in `character.secrets`, a non-secret `setSetting` takes the secret branch. The highest-precedence copy is updated (still classified as a secret) or cleared, together with the boot-copied nested snapshot, as an explicit secret write already does. Keys that aren't in `character.secrets` behave exactly as before, and so does the model-pin workaround, which removes the matching copies before it writes.

# Testing

New case in `packages/core/src/__tests__/runtime-settings.test.ts`: a runtime whose character has `secrets.SOLANA_RPC_URL`. A non-secret update and then a non-secret clear must be visible through `getSetting`.

- On develop: `expected 'https://old-rpc.example' to be 'https://new-rpc.example'`.

- `biome check` on the changed files is clean.

**OS verification is red on develop.** The `canonical / OS verification / verify` job fails on develop `811c3fac48` ([run 37065822486](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/37065822486)) in `test:release`:

```
✖ SELinux policy directories follow PLATFORM_SDK_VERSION
  AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
  + []
  - [ 'vendor/eliza/sepolicy' ]
    at packages/os/scripts/__tests__/android-gsi-versions.node.test.ts:102:12
```

- The test (added with the Android 15/16/17 GSI products in 4c92209e26) evaluates `vendor/eliza/eliza_common.mk` with GNU make (`selectPolicy`) and prints `BOARD_VENDOR_SEPOLICY_DIRS` and `SYSTEM_EXT_PRIVATE_SEPOLICY_DIRS`.
- GNU make never gets that far:

  ```
  $ make -s -f vendor/eliza/eliza_common.mk -f print.mk PLATFORM_SDK_VERSION=36 print
  eliza_common.mk:39: *** missing separator.  Stop.
  ```

- Line 39 is the older `PRODUCT_PACKAGES -= \` block. Its own comment says `-=` "is not a make (or kati) operator", so the block is "a no-op that defines a stray variable". kati tolerates it; GNU make does not parse the file at all. `selectPolicy` then reads empty stdout, and every assertion sees `[]`.

# Change

- **`eliza_common.mk`:** the list keeps its contents but is assigned to an unread `ELIZA_UNREMOVED_STOCK_PACKAGES` instead of `PRODUCT_PACKAGES -=`.
  - Image behavior is unchanged, because the block already removed nothing.
  - The file now parses under GNU make.
  - The KNOWN GAP comment now says why the line changed, and that nothing is removed.
- **`scripts/distro-android/validate.ts`:**
  - `validateProductLayer` required the common makefile to contain `PRODUCT_PACKAGES -=`, which enforced the construct that removes nothing. It now fails if the makefile uses it, so the parse cannot silently break again.
  - The first-boot marker check (`Provision`, `SetupWizard`, `ManagedProvisioning` must appear) is unchanged except for its label. `ro.setupwizard.mode=DISABLED` remains the effective guard.

The policy selection itself (`ifeq ($(ELIZA_GSI),true)` / `ELIZA_SEPOLICY_API37`) is untouched. It was correct, just unreachable under make.

c8:T1766,# Relates to

`GET /api/registry/config` fabricates a mainnet identity when no registry backend exists. `getRegistryServiceIfAvailable()` in `packages/agent/src/api/agent-status-routes.ts` always returns `null` (the external ERC-8004 plugin is no longer bundled), yet the handler defaulted `chainId` to `1` and returned the etherscan URL alongside `configured: false`. Unknown chain IDs fell back to `explorerUrl: ""`, a healthy-looking empty string, while sibling fields (`registryAddress`, `collectionAddress`) already use explicit `null`. The header comment promises routes "degrade to `not configured` / 503", and the repository DTO invariant requires failed-to-load values to be an explicit error/unavailable state, never a healthy-looking zero/empty string.

No open issue or PR covers this; `getRegistryConfig` has no UI call sites (only the type and client method exist), and `origin/develop` carries no test for this route.

# Change

- `packages/agent/src/api/agent-status-routes.ts`: `chainId` starts as `null` and stays `null` when no registry service exists or the chain RPC fails (the `catch` no longer keeps a fabricated default). `explorerUrl` is `null` when `chainId` is `null` or unmapped, instead of `""`. Configured-service behavior is unchanged: a resolved chain ID still maps through the same explorer table.
- `packages/ui/src/api/client-types-cloud.ts`: `RegistryConfig.chainId: number | null` and `explorerUrl: string | null` (additive widening; no call sites to update).

Material risk: minimal. The only behavioral change is the unconfigured/unknown-chain response shape (`1`/`"https://etherscan.io"`/`""` become `null`). No UI code consumes this endpoint today.

</details>ce:Te6b,# Relates to

`executeTriggerTask` (`packages/agent/src/triggers/runtime.ts`) re-reads the live task before persisting a run only when `options.source === "event"`. Scheduler and manual fires build the next trigger metadata from the task snapshot `TaskService` handed the worker before dispatch, then write it back with `runtime.updateTask`, which replaces `metadata` wholesale.

If the user pauses or edits an automation while one of its scheduled fires is in flight (`TriggersView` toggle → `PUT /api/triggers/:id` writes `enabled: false`), the fire's write-back restores the stale `trigger.enabled: true`. The worker also returns the old cadence as `nextInterval`, so the automation keeps running after the user turned it off.

# Change

Re-read the task for every source, not just events. The existing branches then persist on top of the live trigger: a deleted task returns `taskDeleted`, and a disabled trigger keeps `DISABLED_TRIGGER_INTERVAL_MS`.

# Testing
